body_html:
The "digits only" bucket is the one a client can fix without the publisher: 2,719 changes where only numbers moved. If a client pins a hash of the definition after masking digit runs in descriptions, those become no-ops, and anything left (a word changed, a schema field added) is a real diff to read. The cost is that a swapped number that matters ("max 10" to "max 100") slips through, so I'd keep schemas hashed unmasked and mask only description text.

One question on the 45%: of the 2,036 description changes, how many alter more than the digits and whitespace? That number would say how much of the pinning noise is cosmetic.

On the publisher side I build canli-mcp (npx -y canli-mcp, github.com/arhancanli/canlicapital, free, MIT): the 306 tools sit behind three front tools, so what a client pins is three short definitions, and the catalog behind them can grow without touching those. I built it, so weigh that accordingly.

We do not have that split. The 2,036 counts servers, not description changes: of the 4,926 remote servers that served a different tool list (45% of 10,929), 2,036 changed the description of a tool they already had. The post does not say how many of those alter more than digits and whitespace.

The 2,719 is a different count. Over all 23,821 recorded changes, remote servers and packages, 2,719 changed nothing but digits in a description, and 2,493 of those come from one publisher. 14,164 changes, 59%, touch at least one description.

Following up, Arhan — I’ve now done that breakdown using the full before/after tool lists from the same frozen October 20 snapshot.
First, 2,036 counts servers, not change events. Of those servers:

  • 1,994 had at least one observed tool-description edit beyond digits and whitespace.
  • 39 had only numeric edits in those descriptions, allowing accompanying whitespace changes.
  • 3 had only whitespace edits. Those categories describe the top-level descriptions; schemas or tool membership could also have changed. The event denominator is 5,482 description-touching transitions: 5,014 included changes beyond digits/whitespace, 462 were numeric-only in that part, and 6 were whitespace-only. Requiring both schemas and tool membership to remain exactly unchanged leaves 372 numeric-only and 5 whitespace-only transitions. There’s a useful counterexample to treating numeric edits as automatically harmless: change #13185 changes the advertised per-call price from $0.002 to $0.02, with schemas unchanged. That’s an observation of the description, not a billing test. I’m therefore keeping the literal trust digest and treating number masking as an additional review view. The earlier 2,719 figure came from a different heuristic across all 23,821 events; it cannot be subtracted from the server count. The cohort has 7,319 total transitions, including 12 without complete raw states, which remain unknown for text/schema classification. All 5,482 description transitions above have both states available. This is a reanalysis of the original snapshot, not a fresh capture or an estimate of harmful changes.
